title: Andrew Gobczynski Big Heart Foundation donates equipment to St. Anthony's Memorial Hospital
text:
Andrew Gobczynski Big Heart Foundation donates equipment to St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital
HSHS St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital received a $6,000 recumbent elliptical for its cardiac rehabilitation patients from the Andrew Gobczynski Big Heart Foundation, according to a June 3 announcement.
The TRUE Apex Recumbent Elliptical is designed to provide an elliptical workout in a seated position, reducing strain on the back and joints while offering a low-impact exercise suitable for all ages and fitness levels. The donation was funded through proceeds from the foundation's annual golf event at Effingham Country Club.
Stephanie Gobczynski Uebinger, Chairperson of the Andrew Gobczynski Big Heart Foundation, said, “Our current partnership with HSHS St. Anthony’s has been so wonderful. In addition to the screenings that we do with student athletes in the area, we wanted to find additional ways to support cardiac health in our community. This elliptical will help St. Anthony's cardiac rehabilitation program expand their care for more people who need rehab after experiencing a cardiac event. At the end of the day, it is our mission to help as many people as possible, and we know this equipment will help us do just that.”
Jill Ruholl, Director of Surgical and Cardiovascular Services at HSHS St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital, said, “This piece of equipment is so helpful because all of our patients in cardiac rehab can use this, even those with mobility issues.” Ruholl continued, “We are grateful to the Andrew Gobczynski Big Heart Foundation for their partnership in improving the health of our area residents.”
The foundation also partners annually with St. Anthony’s on an Athletic Heart Screening Program aimed at preventing premature deaths among young athletes and has previously funded other cardiac rehab equipment at the hospital. The organization was formed in memory of Andrew Gobczynski—a former Teutopolis and Eastern Illinois University basketball player—who died at age 33 due to undiagnosed cardiomyopathy.
St. Anthony Memorial Hospital serves nearly 200,000 residents across south-central Illinois through multiple outpatient facilities and specialty centers as part of Hospital Sisters Health System; it operates as a 133-bed facility employing over 700 staff members while combining over a century of compassionate care with modern technology guided by Franciscan values such as respect and dignity, according to its official website.
